title: Build a depth-independent rig debug view for skeleton inspection
description:
## User Mandate

> Sythesize these audits of the skeeltal mesh system and then help improve the bone vertex weights. The feet are also no longer flat on the ground, but that's a seperate issue, I think

STRICT. This task concerns skeleton inspection only. Keep foot-grounding behavior separate.

## Summary
Extend the existing skeleton display into a usable rig-debug presentation so pose and weighting changes can be inspected without navigating the generated Unity hierarchy.

## Scope
- Keep `SkeletonDisplay` as a pure data builder.
- Add skeleton-only or faint-mesh mode, depth-independent bone visibility, thicker bone/joint primitives, selected-bone highlighting, labels, and frame/focus controls.
- Synchronize SceneView selection with semantic parts or bones.
- Add a minimal exaggerated pose preview for validating bent-chain rotation and weight deformation.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Bones remain visible through the generated mesh in the debug mode.
- A user can focus the skeleton, selected bone, selected limb, body, and legs without expanding the generated hierarchy.
- Selected bones are distinguishable by shape or thickness as well as color.
- The view exposes stable machine IDs separately from display names.
- Manual Unity editor validation records the controls and result.

## Validation
Run the relevant editor assembly build, focused editor tests, and a manual Unity SceneView check after compilation completes. Record console errors and warnings.

## Findings
The current `SkeletonDisplay` emits line segments and joint points only. The supplied screenshot corroborates a P1 tooling gap, while the display implementation itself remains a useful pure-data boundary.

## Blockers
Unity editor availability is required for the visual gate. This task must not change skeleton inference or weighting ownership.

## Next Step
Add depth-independent rendering and skeleton-only mode first, then add labels, focus, selection, and pose preview.
